extracted.intended_audience: Montana state agency officials, administrative lawyers, legislators, and regulated persons/stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on complying with the Montana Administrative Procedure Act (MAPA) for adopting, amending, repealing, and publicizing administrative rules, including committee review, legislative review, emergency rules, and public inspection requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: "License" definition
rubrics_metrics.description: "License" includes the whole or part of any agency permit, certificate, approval, registration, charter, or other form of permission required by law but does not include a license required solely for revenue purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The "solely for revenue purposes" exemption is intended to exclude licensing that is purely routine or ministerial in nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Licensing" definition
rubrics_metrics.description: "Licensing" includes any agency process respecting the grant, denial, renewal, revocation, suspension, annulment, withdrawal, limitation, transfer, or amendment of a license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The addition of terms such as "limitation", "renewal" and "transfer" clarifies that transactions involving a license as a property right are covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Party" definition
rubrics_metrics.description: "Party" means any person or agency named or admitted as a party or properly seeking and entitled as of right to be admitted as a party; but nothing herein shall be construed to prevent an agency from admitting any person or agency as a party for limited purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The second phrase permits agencies to allow interested persons or agencies who are not sufficiently involved to be parties to appear for limited purposes (comparable to amici).

rubrics_metrics.name: "Person" definition
rubrics_metrics.description: "Person" means any individual, partnership, corporation, association, governmental subdivision, or public organization of any character other than an agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency must adopt description of organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall adopt as a rule a description of its organization, stating the general course and method of its operations and the methods whereby the public may obtain information or make submissions or requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice and hearing requirements of rulemaking do not apply to adoption of a rule describing an agency's organization; the rule describing the organization is typically the first rule in a department's title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency must adopt rules of practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall adopt rules of practice, not inconsistent with statutory provisions, setting forth the nature and requirements of all formal and informal procedures available, including a description of all forms and instructions used by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is meant to correct agencies' lack of procedural rules and to stabilize agency procedures for public guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public inspection of rules and policy statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall make available for public inspection all rules and all other written statements of policy or interpretations formulated, adopted, or used by the agency in the discharge of its functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply constitutional privacy limits where appropriate (e.g., Article II, sec. 9 balancing). Parties should inspect agency policies, decisions and interpretations when agencies lack prior rules or decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy provision and cost recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon request of any person or agency, provide a copy of any rule. Unless otherwise provided by statute, an agency may require the payment of the cost of providing such copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply with the public inspection requirement renders an agency rule not valid or effective against any person or party whose rights have been substantially prejudiced by that failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney General model rules requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The attorney general shall prepare a model form for a rule describing the organization of agencies and model rules of practice for agencies to use as a guide in fulfilling the requirements of 82-4203(1). The attorney general shall add to, amend, or revise the model rules from time to time as he considers necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The model rules should be appropriate for as many agencies as practicable and be filed with the Secretary of State and provided to any agency upon request. Adoption of model rules does not relieve an agency from following formal rule-making procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative review and repeal of rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The legislature may, by joint resolution, repeal any rule in the Montana administrative code. If a rule is repealed, the joint resolution shall state the legislature's objections to the repealed rule. If an agency adopts a new rule to replace the repealed rule, it shall adopt the new rule in accordance with the objections stated by the legislature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The legislature may also direct a change or the adoption of an additional rule by joint resolution, and any such change must be pursuant to statutory authority. A rule remains valid if not repealed before adjournment of the regular session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Code Committee composition, meetings, staff
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative code committee consists of four members of the senate and four members of the house appointed in the same manner as standing committees; it shall meet as often as necessary and may retain employees, consultants, or counsel as necessary to carry out its provisions and advise the publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No more than two appointees of each house may be of the same political party; vacancies outside session are filled by the remaining committee members; members receive compensation and expenses per statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers of the Administrative Code Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee shall review all proposed rules filed with the secretary of state and may prepare written recommendations for adoption, amendment, or rejection; submit oral or written testimony at hearings; require that a rule-making hearing be held; poll all members of the legislature by mail when not in session to determine consistency with legislative intent; and if 20 or more legislators object, poll the members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee must prepare a report to the legislature at least once each biennium and may recommend amendments to MAPA or repeal/amendment/adoption of rules. The committee's authority is primarily advisory but can mandate hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking notice content and publication timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to adoption, amendment, or repeal of any rule, the agency shall give written notice of its intended action. The notice shall include a statement of either the terms or substance of the intended action or a description of the subjects and issues involved, rationale for the intended action, and the time when, place where, and manner in which interested persons may present their views. The notice shall be filed with the secretary of state and mailed to persons who have requested advance notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice shall be published and mailed at least 30 days in advance of the agency's intended action; if any statute provides a different publication method, comply in addition; the notice period may be no less than 30 days or more than 6 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing notice and participation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency shall afford interested persons at least 20 days' notice of a hearing and 28 days to submit data, views, or arguments, orally or in writing. For substantive rules, opportunity for oral hearing shall be granted if requested by either 10% or 25 of the persons who will be directly affected, by a governmental subdivision or agency, or by an association having not less than 25 members who will be directly affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency may continue a hearing date for cause. Contested case procedures need not be followed in hearings held under this section. The agency shall consider fully written and oral submissions, and upon adoption issue a concise statement of the principal reasons for and against adoption, incorporating reasons for overruling objections. The statement of reasons is mandatory and is published in the administrative register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of reasons requirement and adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon adoption of a rule, an agency shall issue a concise statement of the principal reasons for and against its adoption, incorporating its reasons for overruling the considerations urged against its adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A robust statement of reasons demonstrates the agency listened to participants; courts have reviewed adequacy of statements (e.g., Patterson v. State, Dept. of Revenue). The statement is published when the rule is adopted, amended, or repealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency rule adoption criteria and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency finds that an imminent peril to the public health, safety, or welfare requires adoption of a rule upon fewer than 20 days' notice and states in writing its reasons for that finding, it may proceed without prior notice or hearing or upon any abbreviated notice and hearing that it finds practicable to adopt an emergency rule. The rule may be effective for a period not longer than 120 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sufficiency of the reasons for finding imminent peril is subject to judicial review. The Administrative Code Committee advised criteria for 'imminent' (less time than regular minimum), 'peril' (jeopardy of being irretrievably lost), and that 'public' is broader than agency employees or regulated sector. Agencies are cautioned to exercise this power carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity: substantial compliance and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: No rule is valid unless adopted in substantial compliance with subsections (1) or (2) of the rulemaking section and within 6 months of the publishing of notice thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents an agency from relying on stale or forgotten notices to justify later-adopted rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of informal advisory procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may use informal conferences and consultations as a means of obtaining the viewpoints and advice of interested persons and may appoint committees of experts or interested persons or representatives of the general public to advise it with respect to any contemplated rule making. The powers of the committees shall be advisory only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of these techniques does not relieve the agency from following formal rule-making procedures required by MAPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary repetition of statutory language; citation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules may not unnecessarily repeat statutory language. Whenever it is necessary to refer to statutory language in order to convey the meaning of a rule, the reference shall clearly indicate that portion of the language which is statutory and the portion which is amplification of the language. Each rule shall include a citation of authority pursuant to which it, or any part thereof, is adopted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is intended to ensure agency rules do not merely restate statutes and to provide clear authority for rule provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual review of rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall at least annually review its rules to determine if any new rule should be adopted or any existing rule should be modified or repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responds to findings that many agencies go long periods without reviewing or updating rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and statutory consistency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in 82-4203, nothing in this part confers authority upon or augments the authority of any state agency to adopt, administer, or enforce any rule. To be effective, each substantive rule adopted must be within the scope of authority conferred and in accordance with standards prescribed by other provisions of law. No rule is valid unless consistent and not in conflict with the statute and reasonably necessary to effectuate the purpose of the statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MAPA does not create new substantive authority; agencies must ensure rules are consistent with enabling statutes and reasonably necessary to carry out statutory purposes.
